title: Nonfiction needs its own hook
statement: Judge engagement separately for fiction and nonfiction, and give nonfiction its own hook rather than a lower bar, since readers' motivation for the two was not highly associated.
detail: A grade-4 pedagogy definition cites a 2007 study of reading motivation in the later elementary years, which found that students' reading motivations for narrative and information texts were not highly associated, so skill at hooking readers on a story need not carry over to informational text. Because the course is anchored in nonfiction in five of its units, it asks that engagement and craft be scored by genre rather than as one craft score, and that a nonfiction passage get its own hook, such as a real stake, a genuine question or a surprising fact.

evidence.quote: "students' reading motivations for narrative and information texts were not highly associated."
should be checked SEPARATELY by genre, not as one undifferentiated craft score
a nonfiction passage needs its own hook (a real stake, a genuine question, a surprising fact), not a lower engagement bar

citations.ref: Reading motivation and reading comprehension growth in the later elementary years, Contemporary Educational Psychology 32:282-313 (2007)
